text:
Asha (CS): FYI TimberFall hit a sharp p99 spike on /v1/embeddings yesterday afternoon, customers complaining about timeouts. putting this thread for coord.
Tim (TimberFall): seeing a lot of 504s + long tail latency. started around 15:12 UTC, affects embed-create and search routes. sample request-id: rf-9a3c-2b7f. Here's a short repro: POST /v1/embeddings with 12 texts ~ avg len 1.2k chars.
Tim (TimberFall): we rolled back to smaller model (embed-small) earlier and saw partial improvement but still p99 ~ 2.1s (baseline ~0.4s). Any quick action we can take? :worried:
Asha (CS): We opened a support ticket and asked for logs — pinging SRE to help triage whether this is tenant isolation/noisy neighbor or platform throttling.
Devan (SRE): @Maria can you pull the tenant metrics and per-host KV cache hitrate for timberfall-tenant-17? suspect bursty memory pressure causing cache misses. Also want recent per-tenant throttle events.
Maria (Oncall): pulling now.
deploy-bot: Deploy 202-embed-optimizer promoted to prod @ 14:58 UTC on hosts gpux-08..gpux-12
Maria (Oncall): quick snapshot: during 15:10-15:30 UTC -- 95th=450ms, 99th=2.8s for embed-create on region-us-west; throughput for that tenant jumped x6 from baseline. Host gpux-11 shows high swap activity and KV miss rate ~ 62%. Throttle log shows repeated token-throttle entries for tenant=timberfall-17 at ~15:14.
Devan (SRE): OK looks like noisy-tenant behavior (sustained burst > reserved capacity) causing continuous batching to bloat and KV cache churn. Two options for immediate mitigation: 1) apply temporary tenant-level allowlist that pins timberfall to a dedicated small pool or 2) impose short cool-down throttle for that tenant to smooth bursts. Also we can temporarily route their requests to embed-small which has smaller memory working set. Which should we do first?
Asha (CS): Customer prefers availability over throttling. They asked about an allowlist or a reserved burst.
Tim (TimberFall): yes we prefer allowlist/reserved capacity. We can accept a small dedicated pool or temporary higher quota while we investigate.
Devan (SRE): Understood. I'll open a short-lived reservation on Dedicated pool 'reserve-temp-41' (1 GPU small) and set routing policy for tenant=timberfall-17 -> reserve-temp-41 for next 2 hours. Applying now.
Maria (Oncall): command I ran: ```sh
# create reservation
rcli reserve create --pool reserve-temp-41 --tenant timberfall-17 --duration 120m --cap 120rps
# set routing
rcli route set --tenant timberfall-17 --pool reserve-temp-41 --priority 100
```
Maria (Oncall): reservation created and routing applied at 15:42 UTC. I'm also adding an allowlist exception in front of GPU autoscaler to avoid eviction during burst: ```yaml
allowlist:
  tenants: ["timberfall-17"]
```
Devan (SRE): after routing change, observe immediate drop in p99 on gpux-11 from 2.8s -> 520ms within 3 minutes. KV miss rate on that host down to 18%. Good sign.
Tim (TimberFall): seeing much better response now. grateful. Can you tell what triggered the burst? we didn't change traffic intentionally.
Asha (CS): thanks for reporting. We'll do a deeper RCA. Tim, can you share any recent client-side deploys or background jobs that might fan out embedding requests?
Tim (TimberFall): we did a data backfill at 14:50 UTC that reprocessed ~200k records via parallel workers (should have used internal rate limiter but looks like a misconfig).
Devan (SRE): that explains it — big fanout -> bypassed rate limiter -> noisy neighbor. Long-term fixes: 1) enforce per-tenant concurrency limits on bulk jobs via client SDKs and docs, 2) add a soft quota/burst token bucket server-side with better smoothing, 3) expose a self-service reserved-capacity option in console for large backfills.
Asha (CS): immediate follow-ups for us: - Confirmed: reserve applied + routing change reduced tail. - CS to notify TimberFall billing team about short reservation cost. - SRE to create a post-incident task to implement server-side burst smoothing and better telemetry for KV cache churn.
Devan (SRE): creating ticket: PROJ-8472 "tenant burst smoothing + KV churn alerts" and assigning to eng-runtime.
Maria (Oncall): adding a short snippet of the perf delta I grabbed: ```json
{"time_window":"15:00-15:30","p95_before":450,"p99_before":2800,"p95_after":120,"p99_after":520}
```
Tim (TimberFall): thanks all, latency is back to normal on our end. Please keep me posted on the RCA timeline.
Asha (CS): Will do. Closing this immediate action thread — moving to postmortem channel for RCA. :thumbsup:
